@v4d33m is making some headway with the first step of this initiative which is the on chain accounting. After looking at those numbers he and I will have some insights which should help with carrying out this task. 
Some quick remarks but I prefer to do the -$2k intervals without a guarantee of base.
I think in hindsight it makes sense to start after vadim report is delivered

I understand the rationale of the -25% changes per quarter but intuitively I feel that -2k steps will be best.     Please see my other [comment](https://github.com/ubiquity/business-development/issues/152#issuecomment-2721768662).      
I think having several simulations are useful to compare side-by-side though!

Continuing the conversation at https://github.com/ubiquity/business-development/issues/153
Understood these were averages and some months some contributors didn't take base. 
6 FEB 06:00 UTC+9 is when we deployed review incentives which is a big one.
[https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/.ubiquity-os/pull/13](https://www.google.com/url?q=https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/.ubiquity-os/pull/13&sa=D&source=editors&ust=1741922693228134&usg=AOvVaw3X_egE53b1GxQbxQsYaIhV)
This is only used as a placeholder/reference. The accuracy right now is low because: I sampled exactly 2 weeks of data since deploying the "review incentives" a major factor of incentives. Then I multiplied by 2 to get a full month. 
The problem is some contributors didn't collect rewards within this two week span (generally a bad sign) but also there are situations like Eres where they tend to tackle large projects, like one or two per month. Then I rounded to a near whole number, except for Zug because it was such a low number.
We will recalculate all rewards since the beginning of Ubiquity to get totally accurate projections.
I filled this in with very rough projections based on the "post review incentives" rewards. 
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1zAXBiEDopeX3XpOEi33sXz7JIywQ377E8vk4Qac5rSg/edit?gid=829403196#gid=829403196
Looks a bit like the following

I'm sure that when we plug in the latest numbers (@gentlementlegen will get them soon) the net burn should decrease. I guess keeping burn around the same is okay just as long as the high performers are taking home the rewards.
